chunks: And that which was narrated - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Mina when a man entered upon him and said, 'A group of people have arrived today who have missed the Hajj.' He said, 'We ask Allah for well-being.' Then he said, 'I see that each one of them should slaughter a sheep, shave his head, and Hajj will be obligatory upon them next year if they return to their lands; and if they stay until the days of Tashriq pass in Mecca, then they go out to some of the miqat places of the people of Mecca, enter into ihram from there, and perform Umrah, then Hajj will not be obligatory upon them next year.'

So it is understood that if their Hajj was a Hajj of voluntary performance, then Hajj is not obligatory upon them next year; and it is only obligatory upon them if their Hajj was the Hajj of Islam (Fard), according to what we have previously mentioned. And no one should say, 'If it were a voluntary Hajj, he would not have said at the beginning of the report, 'Hajj is obligatory upon them next year if they return to their lands,' because we interpret this as a way of preference and excellence rather than obligation and necessity.' It is also possible that the report is specific to one who stipulated a condition during ihram, for if he stipulated, Hajj is not obligatory upon him next year; and if he did not stipulate, that is obligatory upon him in the coming year. And that which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.مَوَاقِيتُ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ: Miqat places for the people of Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who misses the Hajj pilgrimage?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) ruling on the *Qada* (make-up) of Hajj for those who missed the season, distinguishing between the obligatory *Hajj al-Islam* and voluntary *Hajj al-Tatawwu'*. The text clarifies that while slaughter and shaving are required for the missed year, the subsequent obligation depends on whether the initial Hajj was the first duty or a voluntary one, with scholarly interpretation suggesting the strict obligation applies primarily to the first obligatory Hajj. It also addresses the legal nuance of *takhallud* (stipulating exemption) during Ihram, which can exempt the pilgrim from the immediate make-up obligation if they were prevented from returning.
